exposure: hematologic parameters (Monocyte count, red cell distribution width (RDW), neutrophil/lymphocyte ratio (NLR), monocyte/lymphocyte ratio (MLR), MPV, plateletcrit)
outcome: diagnosis of COVID-19 in pregnant women
cohort: The participants were 39 pregnant women with COVID-19 and 69 healthy pregnant women, all admitted to a high-volume tertiary obstetrics center.
finding: The study found that pregnancies complicated by COVID-19 were not significantly associated with adverse perinatal outcomes, except for an increased C-section rate, and that the monocyte/lymphocyte ratio (MLR) may be a supportive diagnostic parameter for COVID-19 in pregnant women.
mod_finding: An increased C-section rate was observed in pregnancies complicated by COVID-19 compared to healthy pregnancies.
